questions.stem: A patient on lithium therapy developed hypertension. He was on thiazides for hypertension. After few days, he developed coarse tremors and other symptoms suggestive of lithium toxicity. Explain the likely mechanism of this interaction:

options.label: A
options.text: Thiazide inhibits the metabolism of lithium

options.label: B
options.text: Thiazides act as an add on drug to lithium

options.label: C
options.text: Thiazides increases the tubular reabsorption of lithium

questions.answerText: Thiazides increases the tubular reabsorption of lithium
questions.solutionHtml: Thiazides increases the tubular reabsorption of lithium

questions.stem: Resistance to the beta lactams is an alarming and growing phenomenon, in turn, a public health challenge. Therefore out of the following what is the main mechanism of b lactam resistance with b-lactamases:
Pegloticase is used for treatment of:
Which of the following is not a prokinetic?
questions.solutionHtml:
Diphenoxymethane

A prokinetic agent (also gastro prokinetic agent, gastrokinetic agent or propulsive) is a type of drug which enhances gastrointestinal motility by increasing the frequency or strength of contractions, but without disrupting their rhythm.

Prokinetic drug increases gastric emptying, relax pylorus, increases the tone of LES

Examples—

  1. d2 antagonist – metoclopramide Domperidone
  2. 5HT4 agonist –cisapride, prucalopride
  3. Motilin receptor agonist – macrolides

questions.stem: A patient with diabetes and COPD developed post-operative urinary retention. Which of the following drugs can be used for short term treatment to relieve the symptoms of this person?
questions.solutionHtml:
Tamsulosin
  • Bethanechol is a muscarinic cholinomimetic, which acts at cholinergic receptors in the smooth muscle of the urinary bladder.
  • It increases the tone of the detrusor urinary muscle, producing an increase in the intravesical pressure and therefore relieves the acute retention but bethanecol also leads to bronchospasm via M3 receptors present in lungs
  • Tamsulosin is a selective α1receptor antagonist that has preferential selectivity for the α1A receptor in the prostate versus the α1B receptor in the blood vessels.
  • When alpha 1 receptors in the bladder neck, the prostate, the ureter, and the urethra are blocked, a relaxation in smooth muscle tissue results. This mechanism decreases resistance to urinary flow and releases urinary retention and also it doesn’t leads to bronchospasm. Therefore, Tamsulosin is a better answer than Bethanechol.

questions.stem: Drug of choice for invasive aspergillosis:
Which of the following antihypertensive drug is avoided in patients with high serum uric acid levels?
questions.solutionHtml:
Hydrochlorothiazide
  • Hydrochlorothiazide is a diuretic medication often used to treat high blood pressure and edema due to fluid buildup.
  • Hyperuricemia is one of the side effect of hydrochlorothiazide.
  • Thiazide causes hyperuricemia by the following mechanisms -
    1. Hydrochlorothiazide acts by inhibiting NaCl and water absorption in DCT because of which osmotic pressure decreases in the body and because uric acid is osmotic in nature which leads to compensatory reabsorption of uric acid in the body.
    2. Uric acid is absorbed in PCT via a pump URAT1/OAT1 and thiazides also acts via same transporter.

 Therefore, Thiazides competitively block the excretion of uric acid and causes   hyperuricemia.

questions.stem: Which of the following antimicrobials should not be given to a chronic asthmatic patient managed on theophylline therapy?
questions.solutionHtml:
Erythromycin

Erythromycin increases the serum concentration of theophylline because it erythromycin is an enzyme inhibitor and increases theophylline levels and causes toxicity.

questions.stem: A person was given a muscle relaxant that competitively blocks nicotinic receptors. Which of the following drug is used for reversal of muscle relaxation after surgery?
questions.solutionHtml:
Neostigmine
  • Neostigmine is a parasympathomimetic drug which acts by inhibiting acetylcholinesterase enzyme and therefore increases the concentration of Ach in the synapse and reverses the effect of muscle relaxant which competitively blocks the nicotinic receptor.
  • Physostigmine is not used as it is lipid soluble and therefore it will cause CNS side effects while Neostigmine is lipid insoluble.

questions.stem: Anti-glaucoma drug that acts by increasing uveoscleral outflow is :
questions.solutionHtml:
Latanoprost
  • Latanoprost ophthalmic is used to treat glaucoma (a condition in which increased pressure in the eye can lead to gradual loss of vision) and ocular hypertension (a condition which causes increased pressure in the eye).
  • Latanoprost is in a class of medications called prostaglandin analogs. It lowers pressure in the eye by increasing the flow of natural eye fluids out of the eye.

questions.stem: A patient diagnosed with Rheumatoid arthritis was on medications. After 2 years, he developed blurring of vision and was found to have corneal opacity. Which drug is most likely to cause this?
questions.solutionHtml:
Chloroquine

Chloroquine causes bulls eye maculopathy, so patient will have blurring of vision and also chloroquine causes corneal deposits which is responsible for corneal opacity and blindness

questions.stem: A boy is planning to travel by bus. Which of the following drug can be used to prevent motion sickness in this person?
questions.solutionHtml:
Promethazine

Promethazine is an H1 receptor blocking agent. In addition to its antihistaminic action, it provides clinically useful sedative and antiemetic effects.

questions.stem: Which of the following antiarrhythmic drug is contraindicated in a patient with interstitial lung disease?
Which of the following is a late inward sodium channel blocker?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ranolazine
  • Ranolazine inhibits persistent or late inward sodium current (INa) in heart muscle in a variety of voltage-gated sodium channels. Inhibiting that current leads to reductions in intracellular calcium levels. This in turn leads to reduced tension in the heart wall, leading to reduced oxygen requirements for the muscle.
